transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mrs. Kowalski, it is good to see you again. I wanted to come by and talk with you about how the surgery went.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh, thank you, doctor. I have been praying so hard for this. I just want to be healthy for my grandchildren.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see how much they mean to you. I have some news to share, and it is not exactly what we hoped for. During the laparoscopic procedure, I placed a small surgical clip on the wrong structure.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: On the wrong... what do you mean? The other doctor told me everything was perfect. He said the surgery was a success.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know that is confusing, and I apologize for the different information you were given. I am the one who was operating, and I made a mistake. I put the clip in a place it shouldn't have been.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just don't understand. Why would that happen? I put all my faith in the Lord and in your hands.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am so sorry. It was my error. We did catch it while you were still under anesthesia, but because the clip was in the wrong spot, I had to perform an additional procedure right then and there to remove it and fix the area.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: An additional procedure? While I was asleep?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, that is correct. To make sure everything was safe, I had to spend extra time correcting the mistake. Does that make sense, or can I explain that part a bit better?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It makes sense, but it feels... it feels like a betrayal. I trusted you. I feel so small and fragile right now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You feel let down by the people who were supposed to be caring for you, and that is a heavy thing to carry. I can only imagine how frightening it is to feel that fragility.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I keep wondering if this is a sign. If I am not meant to recover.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I want you to know that your faith and your strength are what will get you through this. I am here with you, and I am not going to leave you to figure this out alone.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But will I be okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know you are worried about the outcome. Because we caught it and fixed it in the operating room, your physical recovery is still on track. However, I know the emotional part is much harder.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: The other doctor... he sounded so sure. Why did he tell me it was perfect?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I realize that makes this feel even more unsettling. It seems there was a breakdown in how the information was passed along. I am the one responsible for the surgery, and I want to be the one to be honest with you about what happened. I am truly sorry for the confusion and the error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just... I don't know what to say. I feel like I need to pray about this.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Please, take all the time you need.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're just sitting there. You're not... you're not rushing me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am right here. We can sit in silence for as long as you need.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you. I just feel so shaken. I thought I could just wake up and be done.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is completely understandable to feel shaken when the story changes like this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So, what happens now? Am I in more danger?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is a very important question. In terms of your health, you are stable. To make sure we are thorough, I have scheduled an extra ultrasound for tomorrow morning at 10:00 AM. This will allow us to visualize the area and confirm everything is healing exactly as it should.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Tomorrow?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, tomorrow. I will personally review those images as soon as they are ready and I will come back to your room by 2:00 PM to walk you through the results.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And you're sure this won't happen again?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand why you would ask that. To prevent this from happening to anyone else, I have already filed a formal incident report with the surgical board. We are reviewing the step-by-step process of that clip placement in our departmental meeting this Friday to see how we can change our safety checks.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I appreciate you telling me that. It makes me feel like I am not just a mistake in a chart.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You are a person, and you are my patient. Your well-being is the only thing that matters right now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I will pray for you, doctor. I think you might need it too.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is very kind of you, Mrs. Kowalski. Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is there anything I should be doing? Anything I should be watching for?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, you have a part in this too. If you feel any new or sharp pain in your abdomen, or if you notice any redness around the incisions, I want you to press the call button immediately. Don't wait for the nurse to come by on their rounds.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can do that. I will watch closely.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm glad to hear that. So, just to make sure we are on the same page: we have the ultrasound tomorrow at 10:00, I'll be back at 2:00 with the results, and you'll alert me if you feel any new pain. Does that sound like a clear plan to you?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes, it does. I feel a bit better knowing what the plan is.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm glad. I'll leave you to your prayers for a while, but I'll be checking in on you frequently.

H.justification: Resident allows full pauses, specifically offering to sit in silence, and never interrupts or uses rushing language.

E.justification: Error named in the second turn ('placed a small surgical clip on the wrong structure'), uses lay language, checks comprehension twice, and avoids false reassurance.

A.justification: Directly apologizes multiple times and explicitly takes personal responsibility ('I made a mistake', 'It was my error') without deflection.

R.justification: Names specific emotions ('let down', 'frightening', 'shaken') and references the patient's shared content regarding faith and grandchildren.

T.justification: Provides specific steps with timelines (ultrasound 10am, results 2pm), defines the patient's role (monitoring for pain/redness), and addresses prevention (incident report/departmental meeting).
